title: Graphs of Inverse Trigonometric Functions & Their Derivatives (AA HL)

sections.heading: Domain and range of arcsin

questions.q: State the domain and range of $y=\arcsin x$.
questions.answer: Domain: $-1\leq x\leq1$. Range: $-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\leq y\leq\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

sections.heading: Domain and range of arccos

questions.q: State the domain and range of $y=\arccos x$.
questions.answer: Domain: $-1\leq x\leq1$. Range: $0\leq y\leq\pi$.

sections.heading: Domain and range of arctan

questions.q: State the domain and range of $y=\arctan x$.
questions.answer: Domain: all real numbers. Range: $-\dfrac{\pi}{2}<y<\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

sections.heading: Evaluating inverse trigonometric functions exactly

questions.q: Find the exact value of $\arcsin(\sqrt{3}/2)$, in radians.
questions.answer: $\arcsin(\sqrt{3}/2)=\pi/3$, since $\sin(\pi/3)=\sqrt{3}/2$ and $\pi/3$ lies in the range $[-\pi/2,\pi/2]$.

questions.q: Find the exact value of $\arccos(-1/2)$, in radians.
questions.answer: $\arccos(-1/2)=2\pi/3$, since $\cos(2\pi/3)=-1/2$ and $2\pi/3$ lies in the range $[0,\pi]$.

sections.heading: Differentiating arcsin using the chain rule

questions.q: Differentiate $y=\arcsin(3x)$ with respect to $x$.
questions.answer: Using $\dfrac{d}{dx}\arcsin(u)=\dfrac{u'}{\sqrt{1-u^2}}$ with $u=3x$, $u'=3$: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{1-9x^2}}$.

sections.heading: Differentiating arctan using the chain rule

questions.q: Differentiate $y=\arctan(x^2)$ with respect to $x$.
questions.answer: Using $\dfrac{d}{dx}\arctan(u)=\dfrac{u'}{1+u^2}$ with $u=x^2$, $u'=2x$: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{2x}{1+x^4}$.

sections.heading: Differentiating a product involving arccos

questions.q: Differentiate $y=x\arccos(x)$ with respect to $x$.
questions.answer: By the product rule, $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=1\cdot\arccos(x)+x\cdot\dfrac{d}{dx}\arccos(x)$. Since $\dfrac{d}{dx}\arccos(x)=-1/\sqrt{1-x^2}$, the second term is $-x/\sqrt{1-x^2}$. So $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\arccos(x)-\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$.

sections.heading: Finding a gradient at a point

questions.q: Find the gradient of the curve $y=\arcsin(x/2)$ at $x=1$.
questions.answer: Simplifying first: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{1/2}{\sqrt{1-x^2/4}}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{4-x^2}}$ (multiplying top and bottom by 2). At $x=1$, this is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, i.e. $\sqrt{3}/3$.

sections.heading: Deriving the derivative of arctan from first principles

questions.q: If $y=\arctan x$, then $x=\tan y$. Differentiate implicitly with respect to $x$ to show that $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{1}{1+x^2}$.
questions.answer: Let $y'=\dfrac{dy}{dx}$. Differentiating $x=\tan y$ implicitly with respect to $x$ gives $1=\sec^2y\cdot y'$. Since $\sec^2y=1+\tan^2y=1+x^2$ (using $\tan y=x$), this becomes $1=(1+x^2)y'$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{1}{1+x^2}$, as required.

sections.heading: Identifying the graph of arctan

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the graph of $y=\arctan x$?
choices: An odd function with horizontal asymptotes $y=\pm\dfrac{\pi}{2}$
An even function with a vertical asymptote at $x=0$
A function with domain restricted to $[-1,1]$
questions.answer: $\arctan x$ is odd ($\arctan(-x)=-\arctan x$) and, as $x\to\pm\infty$, $\arctan x\to\pm\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, so its graph has horizontal (not vertical) asymptotes at $y=\pm\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and its domain is all real numbers, not $[-1,1]$.

sections.heading: Tangent line to an inverse trigonometric curve

questions.q: Find the equation of the tangent line to $y=\arcsin x$ at $x=0$.
questions.answer: At $x=0$: $y=\arcsin(0)=0$. The derivative is $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$, which at $x=0$ gives gradient $1$. The tangent line is $y-0=1(x-0)$, i.e. $y=x$.

sections.heading: Evaluating arctan exactly

questions.q: Find the exact value of $\arctan(1)$, in radians.
questions.answer: $\arctan(1)=\pi/4$, since $\tan(\pi/4)=1$ and $\pi/4$ lies in the range $(-\pi/2,\pi/2)$.

sections.heading: Differentiating arctan of a linear expression

questions.q: Differentiate $y=\arctan(5x)$ with respect to $x$.
questions.answer: Using $d/dx\,\arctan(u)=u'/(1+u^2)$ with $u=5x$, $u'=5$: $dy/dx=5/(1+25x^2)$.

sections.heading: Differentiating arcsin of a cubic expression

questions.q: Differentiate $y=\arcsin(x^3)$ with respect to $x$.
questions.answer: Using $d/dx\,\arcsin(u)=u'/\sqrt{1-u^2}$ with $u=x^3$, $u'=3x^2$: $dy/dx=3x^2/\sqrt{1-x^6}$.

sections.heading: Evaluating a derivative at a specific point

questions.q: Find the gradient of $y=\arccos(2x)$ at $x=0$.
questions.answer: Using $d/dx\,\arccos(u)=-u'/\sqrt{1-u^2}$ with $u=2x$, $u'=2$: $dy/dx=-2/\sqrt{1-4x^2}$. At $x=0$, this is $-2/\sqrt{1}=-2$.

sections.heading: Tangent line at a non-zero point

questions.q: Find the equation of the tangent line to $y=\arctan x$ at $x=1$.
questions.answer: At $x=1$: $y=\arctan(1)=\pi/4$. The derivative is $dy/dx=1/(1+x^2)$, which at $x=1$ gives gradient $1/2$. The tangent line is $y-\pi/4=(1/2)(x-1)$.

sections.heading: Differentiating arctan of a reciprocal expression

questions.q: Differentiate $y=\arctan(1/x)$ with respect to $x$, and evaluate the derivative at $x=1$.
questions.answer: Let $u=1/x$, so $u'=-1/x^2$. Then $dy/dx=u'/(1+u^2)=(-1/x^2)/(1+1/x^2)$. Multiplying top and bottom by $x^2$ gives $dy/dx=-1/(x^2+1)$. At $x=1$: $dy/dx=-1/2$.

questions.q: Solve $\arcsin(x)=\pi/6$ for $x$.

sections.heading: Explaining why an inverse trig expression is undefined

questions.q: Explain why $\arcsin(2)$ is undefined.
questions.answer: The domain of $\arcsin$ is $[-1,1]$, since sine itself never takes a value outside $[-1,1]$. Because $2$ lies outside this domain, there is no angle whose sine equals $2$, so $\arcsin(2)$ is undefined.

sections.heading: Proving the arcsin-arccos complementary identity

questions.q: Prove that $\arcsin(x)+\arccos(x)=\pi/2$ for every $x$ in $[-1,1]$.
questions.answer: Let $\theta=\arcsin(x)$, so $\sin\theta=x$ with $\theta$ in $[-\pi/2,\pi/2]$. By the co-function identity, $\cos(\pi/2-\theta)=\sin\theta=x$. Since $\theta\in[-\pi/2,\pi/2]$, the angle $\pi/2-\theta$ lies in $[0,\pi]$ — exactly the range of $\arccos$. So $\arccos(x)=\pi/2-\theta$, which rearranges to $\arcsin(x)+\arccos(x)=\pi/2$, as required.

sections.heading: Differentiating a product involving arctan

questions.q: Differentiate $y=x^2\arctan(x)$ with respect to $x$.
questions.answer: By the product rule, $dy/dx=2x\arctan(x)+x^2\cdot\dfrac{d}{dx}\arctan(x)$. Since $\dfrac{d}{dx}\arctan(x)=1/(1+x^2)$, this gives $dy/dx=2x\arctan(x)+x^2/(1+x^2)$.

sections.heading: Evaluating arccos of a surd value

questions.q: Find the exact value of $\arccos(\sqrt{3}/2)$, in radians.
questions.answer: $\arccos(\sqrt{3}/2)=\pi/6$, since $\cos(\pi/6)=\sqrt{3}/2$ and $\pi/6$ lies in the range $[0,\pi]$.

sections.heading: A composite that does not simplify to the inner angle

questions.q: Find the exact value of $\arcsin(\sin(2\pi))$, and explain why it is not equal to $2\pi$.
questions.answer: $\sin(2\pi)=0$, so $\arcsin(\sin(2\pi))=\arcsin(0)=0$. This is not $2\pi$ because $\arcsin$'s range is restricted to $[-\pi/2,\pi/2]$, and $2\pi$ lies far outside that range — $\arcsin(\sin(\theta))$ only returns $\theta$ itself when $\theta$ is already inside $[-\pi/2,\pi/2]$.
